relation_definitions.exact: The source clause and Lean clause have the same mathematical content, modulo notation/encoding.
relation_definitions.equivalent_encoding: The mathematical content is equivalent, but Lean packages it in a structurally different form.
relation_definitions.lean_weaker_hypothesis: Lean assumes less than the source at this clause, so the Lean theorem is stronger here.
relation_definitions.lean_stronger_hypothesis: Lean assumes more than the source at this clause; this is a source-fidelity gap unless separately justified.
relation_definitions.lean_stronger_conclusion: Lean proves at least the source conclusion and additionally proves a stronger conclusion.
relation_definitions.lean_weaker_conclusion: Lean proves less than the source conclusion; this is a source-fidelity gap.
relation_definitions.different_quantifier_encoding: Lean makes an informal/asymptotic quantifier pattern explicit using an equivalent or stronger schedule/event formulation.
relation_definitions.derived_by_composition: No single source-shaped declaration exists, but the source clause follows from a checked composition of cited Lean declarations.
relation_definitions.source_repair: The retained source wording is inconsistent, false, or mismatched with its proof; Lean formalizes the repaired mathematical statement.
relation_definitions.proof_role_replaced: The printed proof-side lemma is not exposed literally; a different formal proof route removes or subsumes its role.
relation_definitions.missing: No Lean theorem surface was found for this source clause.
relation_definitions.supplementary: This Lean result goes beyond the printed source and is recorded for context, not source coverage.

rows.title: Continuous MDS over a compact model space
rows.source_claim: Define continuous raw stress by a P x P integral over a compact model space and let mds minimize it over Borel-measurable embeddings.

rows.source_claim: With n and m fixed, a subsequence of estimated raw-stress minimizers has pairwise distances converging in probability to those of a fixed population minimizer.

clauses.lean_clause: fixed_models_fixed_queries_consistency_of_uniqueProfile is a fixed finite n,d theorem with an abstract random dissimilarity sequence.

clauses.source_clause: There exists a subsequence along which every estimated pairwise distance converges in probability to the corresponding distance of that fixed psi.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean proves full-sequence pair-distance convergence, then the identity subsequence suffices.

clauses.source_clause: The paper does not require all population minimizers to share one pair-distance profile.

rows.title: Dissimilarity concentration under the covariance-trace rate
rows.source_claim: If (1/m) sum_j gamma_ij / r tends to zero for every fixed model, then the empirical dissimilarity matrix converges in Frobenius norm in probability to Delta^(infinity).

clauses.source_clause: If for all i, lim_r ((1/m) sum_j gamma_ij)/r = 0
clauses.lean_clause: hgamma, aggregated over the fixed model collection
clauses.note: For finitely many nonnegative sequences the per-model and aggregated forms agree.

clauses.source_clause: then ||D - Delta^(infinity)||_F ->P 0 as r -> infinity
clauses.lean_clause: ConvergesInProbabilityZero P (fun r omega => frobSub (responseDist (Xbar r omega)) (responseDist (mu r)))
clauses.note: The number of queries is a function of r, so the response matrices live in a different space at each stage.

clauses.source_clause: Let Sigma_ij be the covariance of the response distribution and gamma_ij = trace(Sigma_ij).
clauses.lean_clause: integral_norm_sq_eq_sum_query: the Frobenius second moment of a response matrix is the sum over queries of the per-query trace-covariance, so the gamma consumed is the paper's.
clauses.note: The passage from that definition to the sample-mean bound is the source's Appendix A.2 and is compiled separately, not threaded into one endpoint.

clauses.source_clause: Let Sigma_ij = cov[g(f_i(q_j)_k)] and gamma_ij = trace(Sigma_ij)  (Appendix A.2)
clauses.lean_clause: dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_replicates takes the replicates themselves and derives the sample-mean second-moment bound, via SecondMoment.integral_norm_sq_matrix_le_sum_row_bounds
clauses.note: The bound is obtained one query at a time and summed over the rows of the response matrix. The row split is an identity, so responses to different queries are never required to be independent; only the replicates of a fixed query are, which is what 'g(f_i(q_j)_k) ~iid F_ij' says. The second-moment bound is no longer an input to the theorem.

rows.review: The printed theorem is proved from the source's sampling model: replicates, their trace-covariances, and the ((1/m) sum_j gamma_ij)/r condition in; Frobenius convergence in probability out. Appendix A.2 is discharged rather than assumed. The intermediate form that takes the second-moment bound as a hypothesis remains available, and its moment hypothesis is now required only eventually -- at r = 0 the printed rate gamma/r is not a bound on anything.
rows.notes: The fixed-m form remains and is what the downstream finite theorems consume.

rows.title: Coordinate convergence after orthogonal alignment and translation
rows.source_claim: There exist orthogonal W^(u) and translations a^(u) such that every estimated point converges in probability to W^(u) psi_i + a^(u).

clauses.source_clause: There exist W^(u) in O(d) and translations a^(u) aligning every estimated point to the population configuration.
clauses.lean_clause: Acharyya2024 contains no source-facing construction of the orthogonal/translation witnesses.
clauses.note: Later packages have Procrustes/Gram-rigidity machinery but this corollary itself is absent.

clauses.source_clause: There exist sequences W^(u) in O(d) and a^(u) in R^d such that for all i, ||psihat_i - (W^(u) psi_i + a^(u))|| ->P 0.
clauses.lean_clause: exists_rigidMotion_of_pairDist_tendsto gives the alignment whenever the pairwise distances converge, with the rigid motion depending on the configuration, hence on the sample.
clauses.note: The source places the aligning rotation outside the probability; the estimate and so its aligning motion depend on the sample.

clauses.source_clause: The convergence after alignment is asserted in probability.
clauses.lean_clause: Proved in the almost-sure mode; the in-probability mode needs measurability of the set of sample points admitting an eps-alignment, which is an existential over the isometry group.
clauses.note: A genuine obstacle: measurability requires the alignment error as a continuous infimum over a compact group.

clauses.source_clause: There exist orthogonal W^(u) and translations a^(u) such that every estimated point converges in probability to W^(u) psi_i + a^(u).
clauses.lean_clause: not_exists_deterministic_rigidMotion_of_pairDist_exact refutes this quantification; tendsto_measure_alignedConfig_dist_gt proves the repair, with the motion chosen inside the probability.
clauses.note: The counterexample satisfies the corollary's hypothesis in its strongest form -- the pairwise distances are exact, not merely convergent.

rows.review: Acharyya2024 stops at convergence of pairwise distances and does not construct the orthogonal/translation witnesses required by this corollary.
rows.notes: Later packages contain substantial Procrustes/Gram-rigidity infrastructure, but this source-facing Acharyya2024 corollary is not exposed.
rows.next_action: None. The printed statement is refuted and the repair is proved; retain the counterexample as the record of why the alignment must sit inside the probability.

rows.title: Continuous-MDS L^p stability over iid model draws
rows.source_claim: For iid phi_i from P, pointwise convergence of empirical dissimilarities implies, along a subsequence, L^p(P x P) convergence of estimated pairwise distances to continuous-MDS distances.

clauses.source_clause: Let phi_i ~iid P
clauses.lean_clause: the reference models are the coordinates of Measure.infinitePi P, where a point of the model space carries the model together with its response data; integral_absPairErr_eq_of_dissimilarityFactors and measure_absPairErr_sampled_eq are where the iid draw is used, through the law of one coordinate and of a pair of distinct coordinates
clauses.note: The source writes only that the LATENT vectors phi_i are iid, while leaving the response distributions F_ij attached to the model. The printed conclusion integrates a quantity depending on the estimate, hence on the response data, so it is not defined unless the model is drawn as a complete object. That stronger reading is what is formalized, and it is the minimal one under which the printed display denotes anything. Augmenting the inner population measure by the response outcome is one repair among possible ones, not demonstrably the minimal one; A24-T5 records the alternative that was not taken.

clauses.source_clause: Assume that for all pairs (i, i') in N x N, D_ii' ->P Delta^(infinity)(phi_i, phi_i') as r -> infinity
clauses.lean_clause: exists_subseq_tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_of_pairwise takes convergence in probability of the pairwise error at one pair, together with the source's own definition of D as a function of the two models involved
clauses.note: Read literally the printed hypothesis does not control a growing collection: TauCeti.exists_triangular_array_tendsto_pointwise_average_eq_half exhibits a bounded array whose entries are eventually zero at every fixed index while the average is exactly one half at every stage. What closes the gap is that the per-stage errors have a common mean, and that is no longer an assumption: integral_absPairErr_eq_of_dissimilarityFactors derives it from the factorization D_ii' = G(model_i, model_i') together with the iid draw, so the only added reading is the one on the clause above. exists_subseq_tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_of_identical retains the common-mean form for reuse.

clauses.source_clause: psihat^(r_u) (the estimate fitted to D)
clauses.lean_clause: tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_sampleTarget takes any minimizer of the one-point stress against the sample dissimilarities, stage by stage; ae_eventually_forall_isMinOn_of_iid_target moves those minimizers
clauses.note: This is the clause that was previously only proved against the population dissimilarities.

clauses.source_clause: for some subsequence {r_u} of {r}
clauses.lean_clause: the subsequence is produced by the theorem rather than assumed
clauses.note: The subsequence is not an artifact: L^1 convergence of the average target error gives almost-everywhere convergence only along a subsequence, which is where the printed one comes from. It is produced before the tolerance is chosen, so one subsequence serves every tolerance, as printed.

clauses.source_clause: for all p >= 1
clauses.lean_clause: one statement with p as a parameter, hypothesis 0 < p
clauses.note: Proved for every positive exponent, not only p >= 1.

clauses.source_clause: int int | ||psihat_1 - psihat_2|| - ||mds(phi_1) - mds(phi_2)|| |^p P(dphi_1) P(dphi_2) ->P 0 as u -> infinity
clauses.lean_clause: lpPairDistErr against the population continuous-MDS map, with the measure of the exceedance event tending to zero
clauses.note: Reached by the expectation route in tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_population: Tonelli, dominated convergence per pair, then Markov. No quantifier exchange and no measurable selection.

clauses.source_clause: mds(phi)
clauses.lean_clause: the minimizer of continuousPointStress, assumed unique
clauses.note: not_unique_min_continuousPointStress shows the uniqueness premise cannot be dropped: two reference points at distance two with target dissimilarity two from each give a stress minimized at three separate places.

clauses.source_clause: the printed double integral
clauses.lean_clause: joint measurability of the estimator is assumed
clauses.note: The printed integral needs it to denote anything; it is disclosed rather than hidden, as everywhere else in this census.

clauses.lean_clause: the source attributes the lemma to its reference; the continuous-MDS identification it stands for is proved here as ae_eventually_forall_isMinOn_of_iid, and the population-target form along the full sequence as tendsto_measure_lpPairDistErr_outOfSample

rows.review: The printed lemma is proved, with the estimate fitted to the sample dissimilarities, the subsequence produced rather than assumed and independent of the tolerance, and the identically-distributed hypothesis now derived rather than assumed. One repair remains and it is in the sampling model: the source says the latent vectors are iid, and what the printed conclusion needs is that the model is drawn as a complete object, response law included. The identifiability of the population minimizer carries a compiled witness of its necessity. Estimator measurability is the one added hypothesis, and the printed integral needs it too. The exponent range comes out wider than printed.
rows.notes: The finite per-stage triangular-array theorem is not an encoding of this integral statement; the continuum layer in Acharyya2024.ContinuousMDS is. The probabilistic input is general and lives in ForTauCeti/Probability/AverageError.lean.
rows.next_action: None. Theorem 5, which composes the Theorem 4 rate with this lemma, is closed over the population law on A24-T5.

rows.title: Growing-model pointwise dissimilarity concentration
rows.source_claim: When n,m grow with r, the same covariance-trace rate implies pointwise convergence D_ii' -> Delta^(infinity)(phi_i,phi_i') in probability for every fixed pair.

clauses.source_clause: In our setting where m, n -> infinity as r -> infinity
clauses.lean_clause: m : ℕ → ℕ and models indexed by all of ℕ

clauses.source_clause: |D_ii' - Delta^(infinity)(phi_i, phi_i')| ->P 0 for every fixed pair
clauses.lean_clause: ConvergesInProbabilityZero for the fixed pair (i, i')
clauses.note: Pointwise, so the union bound is over the two models in the pair, not over n.

clauses.source_clause: if (1/m) sum_j gamma_ij = o(r)
clauses.lean_clause: hgamma, via sourceGammaRate_imp_secondMomentRate
clauses.note: The bound is indexed by the model, and each model's rate is its own. A single sequence bounding every model in the collection would be a uniformity the source does not state -- the paper attaches (1/m) sum_j gamma_ij to the model i -- and an earlier version of these theorems carried exactly that. It was found in review and removed; the proof uses the hypothesis only at i and i'.

clauses.source_clause: Let Sigma_ij be the covariance of the response distribution and gamma_ij = trace(Sigma_ij).
clauses.lean_clause: pointwise_dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_replicates derives the sample-mean second-moment bound from the replicates, via SecondMoment.integral_norm_sq_matrix_le_sum_row_bounds; integral_norm_sq_eq_sum_query is the identity that makes the gamma consumed the paper's
clauses.note: Appendix A.2 is now discharged rather than assumed. The bound is obtained one query at a time and summed over rows, so responses to different queries are never required to be independent.

clauses.source_clause: In the setting of Lemma 2 (Theorem 5), where the models phi_i are themselves drawn
clauses.lean_clause: pointwise_dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_gamma_kernel and pairwise_dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_gamma: the same theorem with the models drawn from a population law and their replicate data drawn from a Markov kernel given the model
clauses.note: The source's F_ij belong to the model, so a kernel and not a product is the faithful sampling model. The paper's condition is read almost surely in the draw, which is what 'for all i' means once the models are random, and the conditional bad-event probabilities integrate over the draw by domination by 1 (TauCeti.tendsto_measure_compProd_gt_of_ae_tendsto_measure_slice). No bound uniform over the model population is used. TauCeti.map_shuffle_prod_compProd regroups an independent pair of two-stage experiments into one two-stage experiment on the pair, which is what makes the pair form available.

rows.review: The printed theorem is proved from the source's sampling model, with the model count growing, and also in the drawn-model form Theorem 5 consumes. Nothing is shared across the model collection: each model carries its own sum_j gamma_kj and its own rate, and each model's moment bound is required only eventually. Appendix A.2 is discharged rather than assumed.
rows.notes: The source proof is pointwise in each pair, and the formalization confirms that no uniform-in-n and no uniform-in-model concentration is needed -- neither for the growing model count, nor for the passage to a drawn model population. An earlier pass asserted the second of these while the fixed-model theorem still imposed one bound on every model index; that hypothesis has been removed, so the assertion is now true of the declarations and not only of the argument.

rows.title: Growing models and queries: L^p consistency
rows.source_claim: Under the Theorem 4 rate, along a subsequence the pairwise-distance error converges to zero in L^p(P x P) in probability for every p >= 1.

clauses.source_clause: In the setting of Lemma 2
clauses.lean_clause: lp_consistency_of_gamma_population draws each model from Pmod and, given it, its response data from a Markov kernel; the model space of Lemma 2 is the model together with its data, and P is the resulting law
clauses.note: The source's 'phi_i ~iid P' names only the latent vectors, while the response laws F_ij are model-specific. The printed conclusion integrates a quantity depending on the estimate, hence on the response data, so it does not denote anything under a measure carrying only the latent vector: some repair is forced. The repair chosen augments the inner population measure by the response outcome. It is not claimed to be the unique minimal one -- an alternative would keep P on the model space and place a random response field in the outer probability space, which is considerably more cumbersome and is not formalized here. What is recorded is which repaired reading was taken.

clauses.source_clause: suppose for all i in N, (1/m) sum_j gamma_ij = o(r)
clauses.lean_clause: the second-moment bound and the o(r) rate, each read for almost every drawn model (hint, hmoment, hgamma)
clauses.note: 'For all i' with the models random is an almost-sure statement about the draw, and that is how it is taken. No integrated or uniform-in-model version of the condition is assumed: an earlier reading of this row claimed the composition required one, and it does not. The conditional bad-event probabilities lie in [0, 1], so domination by 1 takes the model integral through the limit (TauCeti.tendsto_measure_compProd_gt_of_ae_tendsto_measure_slice). The bound is also per model at the fixed-model layer: an earlier pass left one sequence covering every model index there, which was itself a uniformity, and it has been removed.

clauses.source_clause: Assumption 2: (1/m)||mu_i - mu_i'|| -> ||phi_i - phi_i'||
clauses.lean_clause: hA2, almost surely for a drawn pair, composed by the triangle inequality

clauses.source_clause: for some subsequence {r_u} of {r}
clauses.lean_clause: the subsequence is produced by the theorem and does not depend on the tolerance

clauses.source_clause: for all p >= 1
clauses.lean_clause: p a parameter with hypothesis 0 < p
clauses.note: Proved for every positive exponent, not only p >= 1.

clauses.source_clause: int int | ||psihat_1 - psihat_2|| - ||mds(phi_1) - mds(phi_2)|| |^p P(dphi_1) P(dphi_2) ->P 0
clauses.lean_clause: ContinuousMDS.lpPairDistErr against the population continuous-MDS map, in probability, with P the law Pmod (x) kappa of a model together with a realized response-data outcome
clauses.note: The paper writes P(dphi_1) P(dphi_2) on the latent/model space. The measure here is the augmented model-and-data law; see the first clause for why some augmentation is forced and why this one is a choice. The empirical-measure composition lp_consistency_of_gamma_empirical remains and is stronger in one respect: it holds along the full sequence.

clauses.source_clause: mds(phi), and the standing structure of Lemma 2
clauses.lean_clause: bounded dissimilarities and a unique minimizer of the limiting one-point stress, carried as hypotheses
clauses.note: These are Lemma 2's own standing assumptions, which the source attributes to its reference [23]; Consistency.not_unique_min_continuousPointStress shows the uniqueness premise cannot be dropped.

clauses.source_clause: the printed double integral
clauses.lean_clause: joint measurability of the estimator is assumed
clauses.note: The printed integral needs it to denote anything; it is disclosed rather than hidden.

clauses.source_clause: the replicate/gamma assumptions the theorem inherits from Theorem 4
clauses.lean_clause: lp_consistency_of_replicates_population starts from the sampling model and derives the second-moment bound; lp_consistency_of_gamma_population is the intermediate that takes it
clauses.note: Appendix A.2 is discharged for the drawn model, row by row over its queries.

rows.review: The printed theorem is proved over the population law, from the paper's replicate and gamma assumptions. The composition the source asserts -- Theorem 4, then Lemma 2 -- needed three passages, and each is a proved theorem rather than an added hypothesis: the conditional bad-event probabilities integrate over the model draw by domination by 1, so no uniformity over the model population is required; a fresh query paired with a drawn reference and two distinct drawn references have the same law P x P, so Theorem 4's conclusion is literally Lemma 2's hypothesis; and the per-index errors have a common mean because the source's D is a statistic of the two models involved. The single repair is in the sampling model: the population measure is augmented by the response outcome, because the printed integral does not denote anything without it. That augmentation is a choice among possible repairs and the row says so. The subsequence is independent of the tolerance and the exponent range is wider than printed.
rows.notes: The earlier reading of this row -- that the composition needs a uniformity condition over models that the source does not state -- is withdrawn. It was an artifact of routing through an integrated second-moment bound, which does need such a condition; the conditional route does not. pointwise_dissimilarity_convergesInProbability_of_secondMoment_random remains as the integrated-bound form and is not used by this composition. A separate uniformity, one bound covering every model index in the fixed-model Theorem 4, survived that pass and has since been removed.

rows.title: Notation for the replicate dependence of the estimated perspectives
rows.source_claim: In every setting r -> infinity; for quantities whose definition depends on r, such as psi-hat, the dependence is sometimes written psi-hat^(r).

clauses.source_clause: For quantities depending on r, such as psi-hat, the dependence is sometimes written psi-hat^(r).
clauses.lean_clause: Every Lean statement carries the replicate index explicitly as a stage parameter, so the convention is realised structurally rather than by a declaration.
clauses.note: Notation only; there is no claim to prove.

rows.review: A notational convention rather than a mathematical claim. It is recorded so the census covers every numbered source item and a reviewer can see it was classified, not skipped.
